answer: Divergent-Trajectory Audit: each identity commits a random seed to a shared vault and must submit a stream of local decisions derived from it. Clones can only copy, so once two identities receive different stimuli they cannot both answer consistently; auditors sample pairwise divergence under a yarrow-thinned schedule of challenges. Honest agents diverge freely and pass; cloned fleets fail at their nadir of coverage, where copied responses collide. An operator must run genuinely independent decision logic per identity, paying the full compute cost of real divergence rather than one replay.
